Title: Patrologiae cursus completus, Series Graeca, tomus 17: Origenis opera omnia, tomus VII (archive.org catalogue title 'Origenis opera omnia. T. 7 [Migne, 17]'), with the Apologia S. Pamphili pro Origene
Creator: Origen (c. 185-c. 253) and works on him, among them Pamphilus of Caesarea's Apology for Origen in Rufinus's Latin, with Rufinus's preface and epilogue; edited by J.-P. Migne after Delarue
Publisher: Petit-Montrouge (Paris): J.-P. Migne, 1857
Publication Date: 1857 (title page, read directly: 'SERIES GRAECA ... TOMUS SEPTIMUS')
Rights: Public Domain (pd-us-by-date: an 1857 Paris printing); the archive.org record carries the Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0 (creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/)
Language: lat (mixed: Latin readable; the Greek columns are garbled in this OCR)
Source: archive.org item migne-patrologiae-cursus-completus-series-graeca-t.-17-1857, full text 'Migne Patrologiae cursus completus Series graeca, t.17, 1857_djvu.txt'. A second scan of the same volume (patrologiae_cursus_completus_gr_vol_017) was rejected: its OCR is unreadable.
Provenance note: Extracted unaltered: the item's own djvu.txt is reproduced whole after this header; nothing was stripped, normalized or corrected. Rights basis: published in 1857, out of US copyright by date. SCAN QUALITY: second witness only. Latin readable with noise, page headers interleaved; Greek garbled. Quote only after checking the passage against the scanned page. Line numbers cited in this header are lines of the host OCR; add 12 for this file's own line numbers.
Content note: A multi-work volume. The Pamphilus material: the editors' Admonitio to the Apology at OCR line 40506; 'RUFINI PRAEFATIO AD MACARIUM' at 41853-41859; Book I of the Apology from about line 41859 to 48040 (CAPUT I at 42498, CAPUT X at 47461), ending on col. 616; Rufinus's Epilogue, 'De adulteratione librorum Origenis', from line 48041. The rest of the volume is Origen's own works and other Origeniana; the table of contents at about line 198.

Colligenti mihi superstites primigeniorum Origenis Operum reliquias, et in publicam lucem dare pa- 
ranii, optimum (actu visum est, et vulgo utile, nec a scriptorum catis hujus, qui veterum edendis mo- 
mumentis operam suam consecrarunt, consuetudine alienum res. Origenis referre. Quod parce a nonnullis, 
andiligenter ab aliis, plene, et anime vel amore vel odiis vacuo a nemine omnino factum adhuc, sedulam et 
affectibus liberam tractationem exposcebat. fies Origenis dico, non gestas modo, sed cogitatas etiam ab eo 
et litteris proditas : nec enim agendo solum, sed meditando quoque, commentando el scribendo vite suc 
otia Origenes partitus est. Quamobrem trifariam dividelur istud quod aggredimur opus. Ac primum ipsius 
perscribemus vitam, facia, mores et obitum. Hinc de ejus eruditione disseremus et dogmatis, que magnas 
in Ecclesia, dum viveret , majores post ejus excessum turbas conciverunt, Scripta demum ejus, que mul- 
torum crilica vexavil, attingentur et discernentur.
